title: Reproduce
text:
The analysis runs on call-detail records from a Brazilian operator. Those records, and the per-city contact graphs built from them, are confidential and are not in this repository. The code is therefore organised in two tiers.
data/derived/ contains city- and stratum-level aggregates only. No subscriber, node or edge appears in any file.

title: Reproduce
text:
Tier 1
git clone https://github.com/horaciosamaniego/middle-class-brokerage
cd middle-class-brokerage
conda env create -f environment.yml && conda activate brokerage
cd data/derived                 # scripts read and write relative to this folder
python ../../code/make_si_tables.py \
    --position position_summary_population.csv equal-population \
    --position position_summary_area.csv       equal-area \
    --ladder   gf_roles_population.csv          equal-population \
    --ladder   gf_roles_antenna.csv             equal-area \
    --check                     # confirms every value against the paper
The README maps each figure and table in the paper to the script that draws it.

title: Reproduce
text:
Tier 2
The scripts that build data/derived/ from the graphs are in code/ and are documented in the README. They require the per-city .gt graphs and graph-tool.

title: Reproduce
text:
Data availability
Derived city-level data sufficient to reproduce every figure and table are included in this repository and archived on Zenodo. The underlying call-detail records were provided under a confidentiality agreement and cannot be shared.

title: Brokerage without bridging
text:
Main result
Show the code that draws this figure
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "font.size": 10,
                     "axes.edgecolor": "#4F5B61", "axes.labelcolor": "#1B2A33",
                     "xtick.color": "#4F5B61", "ytick.color": "#1B2A33"})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 4.9))
fig.patch.set_facecolor("#FAFAF7"); ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAF7")

ypos = {}
y = 0
for i, (key, label, same) in enumerate(ROLES):
    if i == 3:
        y += 1.3                                   # room for the second group header
    ypos[key] = y
    y += 1

offset = {"equal-population": -0.13, "equal-area": 0.13}
for fname, strat, colour in STRATS:
    if strat not in tables:
        continue
    for key, _, _ in ROLES:
        v = vals(tables[strat], key)
        if not len(v):
            continue
        q1, med, q3 = np.percentile(v, [25, 50, 75])
        yy = ypos[key] + offset[strat]
        ax.plot([q1, q3], [yy, yy], color=colour, lw=2.2, solid_capstyle="round")
        ax.plot(med, yy, "o", ms=7, color=colour,
                mfc=colour if strat == "equal-population" else "#FAFAF7", mew=1.8)

ax.axvline(1, color="#1B2A33", ls=(0, (4, 3)), lw=1)
ax.text(1.005, -1.05, "chance", color="#4F5B61", fontsize=9, va="center")
ax.set_yticks([ypos[k] for k, _, _ in ROLES])
ax.set_yticklabels([l for _, l, _ in ROLES])
for t, (key, _, _) in zip(ax.get_yticklabels(), ROLES):
    if key == "liaison_intermediate":
        t.set_fontweight("bold")                   # the bridging role
ax.set_xlabel("enrichment over chance, $R_\\mathrm{mix}$")
for side in ("top", "right", "left"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)

# group headers, right-aligned with the role labels, one row above each group
for first, text in (("coordinator", "THE TWO CONNECTED PEOPLE SHARE A STRATUM"),
                    ("gatekeeper", "THE TWO CONNECTED PEOPLE ARE IN DIFFERENT STRATA")):
    ax.text(-0.02, ypos[first] - 1.0, text, transform=ax.get_yaxis_transform(),
            ha="right", va="center", fontsize=8, color="#C98A2E", fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylim(y - 0.4, -1.6)                         # inverted: top headroom for headers

handles = [Line2D([], [], marker="o", color=c, mfc=c if s == "equal-population" else "#FAFAF7",
                  mew=1.8, lw=2.2, label=s) for _, s, c in STRATS if s in tables]
ax.legend(handles=handles, frameon=False, loc="lower right", fontsize=9,
          title="income strata", title_fontsize=9)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.40, right=0.97, top=0.98, bottom=0.12)
plt.show()








Figure 1: Brokerage is enriched within strata and absent between them. Enrichment of each brokerage role relative to a null model that holds fixed how much contact each income stratum exchanges. Points are medians across cities, bars the interquartile range. To the right of the dashed line a role occurs more often than chance. Two ways of dividing income into strata give the same picture.

title: Brokerage without bridging
text:
What this means for cities
Research on urban segregation has moved from where people live to where they go and whom they encounter. This result adds a further layer: how contact is arranged. Residents of these cities do call across class lines — most two-step chains of contact link people in different income strata — but no stratum occupies the positions that would carry interaction from one class to the next. A city can therefore look integrated by exposure, or even by its share of cross-class ties, while remaining divided in how those ties are mediated.

This page summarises a manuscript under review. The figure and every number quoted here are computed from the derived data in this repository; full methods, null models, robustness checks and the calibration of the estimator are in the paper and its Supplementary Information. Paper: forthcoming. Archived code and data: Zenodo.
